style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: In a control room, an unstaffed brushed-steel approval-gate panel carrying three separate banks of industrial toggle switches, every switch thrown to the off position, is mounted on a charcoal rack. A single overhead practical lamp from the left rakes across the metal, throwing deep shadows and a long cast shadow onto the concrete floor. Graphite, charcoal and safety yellow palette, 35mm anamorphic wide, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, extreme asymmetry with the panel off-center right and dark rack rows receding left, no people, no text, no logos.
rationale: Cinematic still captures the decisive empty control room where an agent deletion executes with no human present; the three off switch banks directly embody the three defaults, and the wide establishing frame gives environmental weight to an otherwise abstract software failure.
subject: three separate banks of industrial toggle switches on a brushed-steel approval-gate panel, all thrown to the off position in an empty control room.
core_thesis: A fabric's human approval is a default in three places—skill package, tool tag, and host prompt setting—and measured defaults show none of them fires.
core_conflict: Protocol-level recommendation versus app-level default: hosts and servers both point at each other, leaving destructive agent actions unapproved.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the approval-gate panel off-center right, dark rack rows receding left, generous negative space.
alt_text: Three banks of lever switches on a brushed-steel panel, all thrown down, in an empty dark control room.
caption: Three banks of approval toggles sit off in an unstaffed control room while an agent deletion runs.
title: 60.7% Of Agent Deletes Ask Nobody

review.depicts: A dim industrial control room with a brushed-metal panel mounted off-center right, holding three lever switches all thrown to the down position, dark equipment racks receding to the left, and a single overhead lamp casting a light patch on the concrete floor.
review.reason: The three-thrown-switches panel is a direct visual stand-in for the article's three off-by-default approval gates, so a reader would connect the image to the headline's claim that every approval default fails.
